REVISED_2026_07_31.verdict: This checkpoint is WORSE THAN CONSTANT DEPTH on CARLA. It began from depthnet.pt, which scores 0.5268 on the same seal, so the fine-tune destroyed a working model rather than adapting it.
REVISED_2026_07_31.the_training_log_already_showed_it: model photometric error 0.08492 -> 0.18876 at epoch 0, recovering only to 0.16198 by epoch 4 -- it never returned to where it started, and this file already recorded improved_on_carla_init: false and beats_identity: false.
REVISED_2026_07_31.and_the_metric_was_confounded: the CONSTANT baseline moved too, 0.08493 -> 0.18774. Constant depth's photometric error cannot change unless something other than depth changed: evaluate() takes pose_net, which was being trained jointly. A degrading pose network raises every arm at once, so the during-training numbers do not separate depth quality from pose quality at all.
REVISED_2026_07_31.status: This checkpoint should not be used or cited as a self-supervised result. Any future self-supervised adaptation must hold out the ORIGINAL domain and measure it every epoch, against ground truth rather than a photometric proxy that shares parameters with what is being trained.
